title: The Story of Abu Sabir the Patient
summary: Bakhtiyar related the celebrated saga of Abu Sabir:
full_text:
Bakhtiyar related the celebrated saga of Abu Sabir:

'In a border village of Persia lived an honest farmer named Abu Sabir—whose name meant "Father of Patience." A tyrannical local governor plundered his cattle, burned his farmhouse, and drove him with his wife and children into exile. While his companions urged him to rebel or curse his fate, Abu Sabir replied calmly: "Patience is the key to deliverance; the wheel of time turns, and truth shall prevail."

In a foreign city, he took service as a laborer in a royal quarry. When an unjust overseer struck him falsely, Abu Sabir did not retaliate, but worked with quiet diligence, winning the love of all the workers.

A sudden revolution broke out in the capital: the old tyrannical dynasty collapsed, and the citizens, seeking a ruler whose character was untainted by cruelty, greed, or factional hatred, looked for the most just man in the realm.

The quarrymen, the merchants, and the elders came forward unanimously, pointing to Abu Sabir: "Here is a man who suffered every injustice without losing his gentleness, and who possesses the patience to govern an empire!"

Abu Sabir was crowned King amidst the cheers of the nation.

When the former oppressive governor was captured and brought before his throne in chains, expecting execution, King Abu Sabir descended from his dais, struck off his chains, and said:

"I conquered your oppression through thirty years of patient virtue; shall I now imitate your cruelty? Go in peace, and learn that patience is a stronger fortress than all your iron spears."'
moral: Unshakeable patience and refusal to seek vengeance transform a persecuted exile into a beloved king.
